unit.title: Databases and SQL for school records

lesson.title: Asking questions: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY
lesson.subtitle: Pick columns, pick rows, sort, and check the answer

video.title: Asking questions: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (main character)
Mr Joseph — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Six A; Maths under 10; 400 pupils. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Before the parents' evening, I need every pupil in Six A with a maths mark under ten. Our school has four hundred pupils in one big sheet. Scrolling? No thanks.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.on_screen_text: Asking questions: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY
scenes.narration: Today: asking the database questions with SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT name, class … Caption: Columns after SELECT, the table after FROM
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Every question starts the same way. SELECT says which columns you want back. FROM says which table to look in. And a star means every column.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT name, mark … Caption: Text in single quotes; AND needs both
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: WHERE picks the rows. Equals, greater than, less than: class equals six A, mark less than ten. Text goes in single quotes, and it must match exactly. AND needs both to be true; OR needs either one.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT name, mark … Caption: Biggest first, then the first three rows
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: ORDER BY sorts the answer. Add DESC for the biggest first. And LIMIT keeps only the first few rows: the top three, say.

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Describe the rows; The database finds them; 12 rows or 12 million.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A query: a question in SQL
scenes.narration: That's a query: a question in SQL. It describes the rows you want, not how to find them. The same query works on twelve rows or twelve million.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Which part of a query picks which rows come back?

scenes.visual: Two columns: “SELECT” (Picks the columns) and “WHERE” (Picks the rows).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: WHERE picks the rows; SELECT picks the columns. Keep them apart in your head: columns across, rows down.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Nobody? '6A' isn't '6a'; Half the school? A missing condition; Compare with what you know.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Check it against what you know
scenes.narration: Always check an answer against what you know. If WHERE class equals six A returns nobody, look at the data: maybe it says six small a. If a query returns half the school, a condition is missing.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Pick a question; Change it; Run it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: ask the school database
scenes.narration: In the app, real SQL runs on your phone, on a school's pupils and marks. Pick a question, change it, and run it. Try changing five B to six A, or AVG to MAX.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. I want the three highest maths marks, biggest first. Which lines do that?

scenes.visual: Summary card: SELECT columns, FROM a table; WHERE picks the rows; ORDER BY, then LIMIT; Check against what you know. Takeaway bar: Describe the rows you want; the database finds them.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: ORDER BY mark DESC, then LIMIT three. Remember: SELECT picks columns, FROM the table, WHERE the rows. Text goes in single quotes, matched exactly. And check every answer against what you already know.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A card per pupil: the rows; Read out a query; Matches step forward, in order. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play “Human database”. Each pupil holds a card with their class, birth month and how they travel. Read out a query: select pupils where travel is walking, order by birth month. The pupils who match step forward and line up in order.

checkpoints.prompt: Which part of a query picks which rows come back?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — WHERE keeps only the rows that match its condition. SELECT picks the columns.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — SELECT picks the columns and FROM the table. WHERE picks the rows.

checkpoints.prompt: You want the three highest maths marks, biggest first. Which lines do that?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — DESC puts the biggest first, and LIMIT 3 keeps the first three rows.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — without DESC, ORDER BY puts the smallest first. WHERE mark = 3 finds marks of exactly 3.
